The URL routes accept only http:// and https:// (devtools:// and chrome:// no longer load, 400); ExifTool no longer loads ~/.ExifTool_config and the metadata keys j, addtagsfromfile and alltagsfromfile are refused with 400 (a crafted metadata key could plant a config file that ExifTool then ran as Perl); path and wss:// deny rules now also apply to WebSocket handshakes; the compromised eMudhra roots are dropped; Chromium 156.0.8078.47; Go 1.27.3 and pdfcpu 0.16.3 (HIGH CVEs in the Go standard library). Digest sha256:13672f317b443c793e972b1bd2155ec62a3e7b6891b411e8196442cc053ee5f5. 2026.11-rc27 (security-mandatory, #3308): 8.39.0 -> 8.40.0, the last Gotenberg 8 release. Fixes GHSA-r77c-ghhj-665p (unauthenticated file read) and GHSA-cfqv-cv4g-hw85 (Chromium trusted the compromised eMudhra roots until its component updater ran; a managed policy now distrusts emSign ECC Root CA - G3, emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services at startup); QPDF encryption passwords can no longer inject an argument file; the private-IP checks refuse more special-purpose ranges (0.0.0.0/8, 192.0.0.0/24, 192.88.99.0/24, 240.0.0.0/4 and several IPv6 blocks); WebSocket connections go through the pinning proxy. Chromium 156.0.8078.79, LibreOffice 26.8.2. Behaviour changes checked against our use: an invalid --chromium-host-resolver-rules now stops the start - the offline overlay's rule (MAP * ~NOTFOUND , EXCLUDE localhost , EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1) was started on 8.40.0 and converts HTML to PDF; --chromium-proxy-server with outbound policies warns (not set); linux/386 needs seccomp=unconfined on Docker 29.4+ (not shipped). The existing --chromium-deny-private-ips and --chromium-deny-list flags are unchanged in 8.40.0. Digest sha256:53073e798c8ef39ea2187e44cb67bab77894ea2509100b94c4fe3b461f7b2996.

It is `pull_policy: never` in both modules/llm/compose.yml and compose.no-build.yml (see tests/unit/consistency/test_270_no_private_registry.py), so it is NEVER fetched over the network by any box — only a local `docker build` (modules/llm/gpustack/Dockerfile.vulkan; see custom_built.razzfazz-gpustack) or a `docker load` from an offline package (Enterprise). Historical SBOMs under releases/ keep the old name on purpose — they record what actually shipped.
